Faded Castle (also: The Faded Castle, golden castellum): The Faded Castle is a sunken ruin in the Nostoi Region that was once part of ancient Remuria. The Harmosts and scholars of Remuria lived there, maintaining archives and researching music theory and fate. The castle holds the portal to the Sea of Bygone Eras, an even deeper region where the main Remurian ruins lie. The Traveler first enters it during the 4.6 World Quest The Shadow Over Petrichor.

In Cassiodor's words it was the "golden castellum", where he and many companions recorded old plays, music scores and every story, real or imagined, in the hope of using them to master fate. Later the castle became the base of Boethius's Golden Troupe. Cassiodor, who sealed it to protect Fontaine, is the one who lets the Traveler in.

Geography: The castle has several levels: an upper level, a middle level, a lower level with a pool, and an exhibition hall. Paintings of Domus Aurea hang in the middle level. Stages and murals use the power of the symphony, and the way into the Sea of Bygone Eras is a portal in the castle.

People: The Harmosts, including Cassiodor, lived and worked here. The cat Osse is Cassiodor's spirit, speaking from the present. Boethius appears as a shadow rising from the mural. Praetorian Golems guard it.

History: In Remuria's golden age the Harmosts kept records of plays, scores and stories here. After the empire fell, Boethius gathered the survivors of Remuria into the castle as the Golden Troupe to resurrect the dead empire. Cassiodor opposed him, because the plan meant destroying the new nation of Fontaine and stealing its people's souls, and sealed the passage to the surface.

Cassiodor says he and his colleagues lived here when a new nation had just been born and "the possibilities were yet endless", organising the classics and researching music theory and magic to tame its perilous power. Item text for the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box, as cited on the wiki, says Boethius's survivors gathered here to research reviving the empire.

Quests: The Shadow Over Petrichor leads the Traveler to the castle; Underwater Nocturne is set inside it. The player collects grimoires, a blank score and performs the symphony on the mural, which produces the score Tuba Mirum.

Status as of 7.1: The castle is now open. The seal is gone, and Phobos has been silenced, so the portal leads to quiet ruins.

Unsolved: its role in the Golden Troupe's history is only hinted at.

67.content: Unsigned notes by a Harmost behind a bookshelf by the lower pool, partly based on the real treatise De institutione musica. They classify music into three kinds: Musica Mundana, the order of everything, Musica Humana, the music of mortals and gods, and Musica Instrumentalis, played by instruments. The writer links the first to Fortuna and says mortals and gods can replace the world's music with their own, and that musicless people cannot be considered human. The notes mention that Euergetia will explain astrological signs.

68.comment: Faded Castle: Investigation of the Northern Barbarians
68.content: Report by Hirtius, vicarius of Legio VI Rithimi Versi, on the tribes of the northern border, for the use of future officers. Marius Servius adds notes. It records the "Mistress of All Waters" as a label forced on diverse gods by Aremorica's leader and contains many erased pages.

key: The Fall of the Faded Castle
69.comment: Faded Castle: The Fall of the Faded Castle
69.content: Three poems in a book with this title, found in Fontaine from Version 4.2. They tell of a black ship and a dark-robed figure, a golden castle by a lake with a frightened master, and a red fog from which its guests and master fall. They read as legend rather than record, and the wiki ties the master to Boethius and the bees to Phobos.

70.content:
Faded Theater: Faded Theater is an artifact domain in Petrichor, in the Nostoi Region of Fontaine. Its flavor text says that the prophet and the ruler, heroes and fell dragons, the grand opera of the golden age once played out here; now the only players on the stage are monsters of unknown provenance.

Clearing it grants artifacts: Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy, Unfinished Reverie, Brave Heart and Scholar.

Geography: A ruined theater-stage in Petrichor within the Nostoi Region.

History: Fontaine's golden-age opera, as the domain frames it, was staged here with a prophet, a ruler, heroes and dragons as characters.

Dangers: Rock Shield hilichurls and Mitachurls, slimes and Pyro Shooters, with Praetorian Golems as the strongest foes.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent artifact domain as of 7.1, added in 4.6; no story events are tied to it.

71.content:
Fleuve Cendre (also: Court of Fontaine: Fleuve Cendre, Ashen River, Fleuve cendré, the undercity of Fontaine): Fleuve Cendre ("Ashen River") is the undercity of Fontaine: a damp, poorly lit settlement in the sewers beneath the Court of Fontaine. Societal outcasts live here: ex-convicts, active criminals, the destitute, orphans and manual labourers whom the surface no longer needs. The Court of Fontaine has long treated it as a grey legal area outside its jurisdiction. Today the Spina di Rosula, led by Navia, is its de facto government.

It is the home district of several well-known Fontainians: Navia, Freminet, Chevreuse and the champion duelist Marfisa are all said to have been born or raised here. Many residents served time in the Fortress of Meropide and came here for a fresh start, sometimes with their families.

Geography: A sewer-level settlement with little sunlight, poor air circulation and cramped living space; the air is dirty and damp. It lies below the Court of Fontaine and is reached from two access points in the Court: one beside Cafe Lutece on the west side and one across the street from Damoville Purveyor on the east.

Places: L'or noir is a bar owned by the Spina di Rosula; its bartender Tetreaux also helps residents with supplies and household matters. A message board there carries local notices. There is a general goods store (Bracari) and a travelling merchant (Crossa), and a doctor, Areta.

People: Open-world residents include Areta (doctor), Bracari (store manager), Tetreaux (bartender), Lelienne, Aurele, Hugues, Lisette, Verut, Vitruvia, Faustier, Potier (seen at night) and the Spina's Consigliere. After the world quest A Fontainian Message, the Spina enforcers Luca ("The Fisherman") and Sonny ("The White Glove") appear here.

Governance: Historically the Court of Fontaine had no real jurisdiction here. The Spina di Rosula now mediates conflicts, manages relations with the Court and keeps order. Residents say it watches everyone "like hawks"; illegal funding is harder to find, and anyone who starts an armed fight can be "sent away to start a new life in the ocean" by the Spina.

Culture: Poor but close-knit. Parents are often too busy making ends meet to watch their children, who are left to their own devices. Most people keep a weapon, often a gun, and few bother to hide it. Locals are wary of outsiders and quick to say that anything left in the open will be stolen.

History: Hundreds of years ago, to "improve" the city, the Court of Fontaine turned its sewers into an undercity for society's "shadows". Many manual labourers ended up here as technology reduced the demand for their work. The early inhabitants believed their diligence might win them the right to live on the surface and turn the Ashen River into somewhere as beautiful as the world above.

Dangers: Weapons are common, theft is routine, and violence is a daily possibility. Armed conflict is discouraged and punished by the Spina, so most trouble is petty or hidden rather than open warfare.

Travel: Enter through the two access points in the Court of Fontaine (beside Cafe Lutece, and across the street from Damoville Purveyor). Fleuve Cendre has its own teleport waypoint underground.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fleuve Cendre remains a poor, damp undercity under the Spina di Rosula's watch. No later canon changes its state.

The Court of Fontaine still does not manage it directly. Navia continues to lead the Spina from Poisson and the Court, and its members still run L'or noir and the local relief work.

72.comment: Fleuve Cendre: Eduardo Baker and the Purge of Fleuve Cendre
72.content: Eduardo Baker was an outlaw leader of Fleuve Cendre before the cataclysm. He protected merchants from gangs, settled local disputes and blessed newlyweds, using a bronze pipe he called the "Ferryman". He was among those arrested in the purge of Fleuve Cendre and was being taken to exile in the desert when his henchmen freed him. The wiki adds that he ran taverns in Fleuve Cendre where the stage performers who became Parsifal the Great (and her sister Josephine) got their start. His son Jakob (later Jakob Ingold) was born there.

73.comment: Fleuve Cendre: The Spina di Rosula in Fleuve Cendre
73.content: The Spina di Rosula is a citizens' organisation of Fontaine that helps ordinary people and investigates matters the Gardes will not or cannot handle. It was founded by Callas and is now led by his daughter Navia. In Fleuve Cendre it runs the bar L'or noir, a stronghold and relief services, and is the practical authority.

74.content:
Foggy Forest Path (also: Foggy Forest Path subarea): The Foggy Forest Path is a subarea in the southern part of Erinnyes Forest, by the water, where mist hangs among the trees and a glowing blue tree stands out. It is the setting of the world quest "Foggy Forest Path", part of "The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes", added in Version 4.2.

The path is hinted at by inscribed stone tablets at Marcotte Station. At its end an altar, three reed-pipe puzzles and a tree lead to a meeting with a Melusine called Pahsiv.

Geography: Located at the southern edge of Erinnyes Forest beside the water, the path is shrouded in fog. A large tree with a blue glow dominates the area, and an altar stands near it. The surrounding forest belongs to the wider Erinnyes Forest, which has its own entry.

Places: Carved stone tablets at a fountain in Marcotte Station, scratched out except for a few words mentioning "clear dew" and the Foggy Forest Path. The Mysterious Altar deeper in, whose inscription is likewise defaced and mentions "clear dew" and "three". The glowing tree, on which three orbs appear once the altar's puzzles are done.

Quests: In "Foggy Forest Path" (4.2), Paimon notices the damaged tablets at Marcotte Station and hopes for hidden treasure. The Traveler completes three Harmonious Reed Pipe puzzles in the area, which makes three orbs appear on the tree. The item on the altar proves to be a drop of water, and a Melusine speaks to them, using only the words "Pahsiv" and "Melusine". Paimon works out that "Pahsiv" means yes and "Melusine" means no, and since the Melusine likes the name, Paimon calls her Pahsiv. She also says "Erinnyes". The quest leads on to "Within the Depths of Erinnyes".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is unchanged and accessible.

75.content:
Fontaine (also: Nation of Justice, Fontainian): Fontaine is the nation of Hydro and justice, a "terrestrial sea" on a raised plateau at the centre of Teyvat, said to be the source of all the continent's waters. Its capital, the Court of Fontaine, is a Belle Epoque-style city of fountains, aquabuses, clockwork meka and theatres, and Fontainians pride themselves on art, elegance and technology. Trials at the Opera Epiclese are public spectacle. Since 4.2 Fontaine has had no Archon: the Iudex Neuvillette, secretly the Hydro Dragon, runs its affairs.

The nation once worshipped the Hydro Archon (Egeria, then Focalors, whom the public knew as Furina). For five hundred years it lived under a prophecy that its people would dissolve into the sea; that crisis was resolved in the Archon Quest "Masquerade of the Guilty". Other peoples live here too, notably the Melusines, and the Oceanids once did.

Geography: The whole continental plate is elevated well above neighbouring nations and edged by a waterfall thousands of metres high. Areas: the Court of Fontaine Region (the capital, the island of Erinnyes with the Opera Epiclese), the Belleau and Beryl Regions (the mountain-sized remains of Elynas, with Merusea Village beneath), the Liffey Region (Fortress of Meropide offshore), the Fontaine Research Institute Region, the Morte Region and Erinnyes Forest, and in the south the Nostoi Region (Petrichor) and the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Government: The Palais Mermonia, at the highest point of the capital, is the seat of all administration and effectively the highest authority. It houses the Maisons: Ordalie (the judiciary, headed by the Chief Justice or Iudex, Neuvillette), Gestion (documents and administration), Cardinalice (financial approvals) and Gardiennage (law enforcement, with the Gardes and Gardemeks). Even when Furina reigned, the real work was done by humans and Melusines in the Palais. Since her abdication Neuvillette handles all affairs that once belonged to the Archon's title.

Religion: Fontaine worshipped the Hydro Archon, God of Justice: first Egeria, the "Mistress of Many Waters", and then Focalors. For five centuries the public face of the god was Furina, flamboyant and theatrical, who sat in a box at trials. There is a Statue of the Seven inside the Court of Fontaine itself; Snezhnograd is the only other main city with one. Since 4.2 there is no Hydro Archon and the throne cannot be refilled.

History: After an ancient flood drowned the first civilisation, the god Remus founded Remuria, a musical empire ruling the waters, which sank about 2,000 years ago. Egeria then became Hydro Archon, united the surviving tribes and gave Fontaine its laws. By turning Oceanids into humans with Primordial Seawater she committed a "sin" in Celestia's eyes, and a prophecy foretold that Fontaine's people would dissolve back into the sea. Egeria died in the cataclysm 500 years ago; her successor Focalors spent five centuries on a secret plan, fulfilled in 4.2.

Customs: Trials are theatre: citizens buy tickets to watch prosecution, defence and twists at the Opera Epiclese, which also hosts magic shows and plays. Fontainians love newspapers, gossip, fashion, film and fine food. The Fontinalia Festival, honouring the Lochknights, once had people in costume raise golden cups and ask door to door for pure water; Furina turned it into a carnival where children shout "Trial or treat!" for candy.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fontaine is at peace and has no Archon. In 4.2 the real Hydro Archon, Focalors, executed herself through the Oratrice, destroying the Hydro Archon's throne; Neuvillette regained the Hydro Dragon's authority and absolved Fontainians, who no longer dissolve in Primordial Seawater. Furina abdicated and now lives as an ordinary actress and director. Neuvillette runs the nation and judges trials himself.

The Oratrice no longer works. The Hydro Gnosis went to Arlecchino, and the Fatui hold it. Under her later deal with Neuvillette, the Fatui scale back operations while former House of the Hearth members are left alone. In 6.7 the Harbinger Sandrone, revived at the Research Institute, briefly ran the Wingalet before returning to Snezhnaya; the Archon Quest is now in Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1).

76.comment: Fontaine: Court of Fontaine and Erinnyes
76.content: The Court of Fontaine was the court of the God of Justice and is now under Chief Justice Neuvillette. The Palais Mermonia, at its summit, holds Neuvillette's office, the Maisons and Furina's former residence. Districts include Quartier Lyonnais, Quartier Narbonnais (The Steambird's offices), Vasari Passage and the poorer lower quarter, Fleuve Cendre. The Opera Epiclese stands on the island of Erinnyes, reached by the Navia aquabus line via Marcotte Station; a lift behind it descends towards the Fortress of Meropide.

77.comment: Fontaine: The Opera Epiclese and the Oratrice
77.content: Fontaine's main courthouse is an opera house. Trials there are public performances with tickets, and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a giant mechanical scale behind the judge's seat, used to deliver the final verdict, which the Iudex had to honour. It also turned the audience's belief in justice into Indemnitium, powering lamps and transport in the Court and Erinnyes.

78.content: An autonomous undersea stronghold off the Liffey Region that serves as Fontaine's de facto prison and largest meka factory. Convicts are technically exiles; the Court only lends some Gardes. Inmates work for Credit Coupons, which replace Mora inside. Its Administrator, "the Duke", is Wriothesley, a former inmate who took the post after the previous administrator fled the duel Wriothesley had challenged him to; Sigewinne runs the infirmary.

79.content: Beryl, across the water from the Court, is an ancient ruin-studded range where Egeria's followers once held picnics. Liffey holds the waters around Meropide and the Research Institute region its floating ruins. Morte ("dead") Region holds the Tower of Ipsissimus, and Erinnyes Forest (4.2) is a misty woodland. Romaritime Harbor is the main port.

80.content: Elynas was a colossal beast that brought pollution to Fontaine during the cataclysm and was mortally wounded by the Fontaine Armada; its skeleton is now a mountain ridge in the Beryl Region, with Merusea Village hidden underwater inside it. The Melusines, a small amphibious all-female species, were born from its wounds about 400 years ago. Neuvillette brought them into society, where many work in the Marechaussee Phantom; they see him as their ideal father.

81.comment: Fontaine: Remuria and the God King
81.content: Before Egeria, the god Remus, who came from Sumeru after Gurabad's fall, founded Remuria above Fontaine's waters, teaching farming, building and above all music. His capital was Capitolium and his emblem the golden bee. Prophesied to perish utterly and return to the Primordial Sea, Remus purged Lochfolk, vishaps and "barbarian" tribes, shared power with four Harmosts and poured his people's souls into golem bodies of stone and golden Ichor. Remuria sank anyway; its ruins lie in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

82.comment: Fontaine: Egeria, the Oceanids and the Original Sin
82.content: Egeria was created as the new heart of the Primordial Sea after the Heavenly Principles took the Hydro Dragon's authority. Oceanids, said to spring from her tears, spread across Teyvat; when some longed to live on land, she poured Primordial Seawater into their veins, making them human. Celestia judged this unauthorised creation of life a sin, imprisoned her for a time and condemned her people. After Remuria's fall she ruled as Hydro Archon, then died at Tunigi Hollow in the cataclysm, her body becoming the Amrita.

83.comment: Fontaine: The Prophecy and Focalors' Plan
83.content: The prophecy said every Fontainian is born guilty, the waters will rise, the people will dissolve, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne. Focalors split herself: her divinity hid in the Oratrice while her humanity, Furina, played the Archon publicly for about 500 years without being told the full plan. In 4.2 Furina was tried and exposed as an ordinary Fontainian; the Oratrice then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death and Focalors executed herself, destroying the throne.

84.content: The Knave, Arlecchino, head of the House of the Hearth orphanage in Fontaine, pressed Furina about the prophecy and once attacked her to check whether she carried the Gnosis, an encounter that left Furina traumatised. Her Fatui helped evacuate Poisson and build the "magic box" used to stage Furina's trial. Afterwards Neuvillette gave her the Hydro Gnosis.

key: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region
85.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region
85.content:
Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region (also: Kinetic Energy Engineering Region): This is the area where the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering stands. Years ago the Institute's central laboratory was largely destroyed in an explosion linked to Edwin Eastinghouse's research into Arkhium, leaving huge Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies floating in the air. The organisation now works from a nearby New Fontaine Research Institute.

The region's boss is the Experimental Field Generator. The map blurb 'Variation of Debris and Metal' describes a pursuit of salvation that suddenly stopped, and an adventurer who never rests whether the destination is a castle in the sky or a deep-sea canyon.

Geography: The region lies on the northern side of the island of Erinnyes, next to Erinnyes Forest. It has the old Central Laboratory ruins, the New Institute and a scatter of former institute buildings: dormitories, an Institute of Clockwork Applications, an Executive Office, a Materials Office, an Academic Assembly Hall and a Game Venue. Dryas Wood is a small hollow between the Institute and Erinnyes Forest.

Places: - **New Fontaine Research Institute**: the Institute's current seat since the explosion. It was formerly known as the Alain Guillotin Research Institute and hosted weekly lectures on critical projects.
- **Central Laboratory Ruins**: the wrecked heart of the old Institute.
- **Dryas Wood**: the Institute's old 'backyard' of plant nurseries; the potioneer who made 'Pure Water' is said to have lived in seclusion here.

People: Researchers, technicians and administrators of the Institute. According to the faction page, the co-administrators Raimondo and Choiseul now run it and Augustus Lovelace says it was a paradise for researchers before they took over. Edwin Eastinghouse, a Senior Technician, made the Prototype Cal. Breguet series of Clockwork Meka.

Culture: The Institute studies machines and energy; many inventions of Fontaine, including clockwork mechanisms and kinetic cores by founder Alain Guillotin, come from it. Unlike the Sumeru Akademiya it does not educate or administer the public. It is controversial: Elphane finds its technicians' lectures ghastly, and the Mekafish it built to clean the water ended up killing fish, which Linorea resents.

History: One of the Institute's main aims was to find answers to the prophesied flood, and researchers believed harnessing Arkhium to defy gravity was the key. Eastinghouse's field generator overloaded, destroying most of the Institute and hurling blocks of water and ruins into the sky. After this the Institute rebuilt nearby and the Callas Line aquabus route was shut down.

Atmosphere: Wrecked laboratories with huge blocks of water hanging overhead. The quest describes dealing with the new Institute's administration as a long, mind-numbing procedure.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers, Clockwork Meka, Fontemer Aberrants, hilichurl camps, Frost and Wind Operatives and the Experimental Field Generator. In the quest, a second explosion scatters components of the large Arkhium inhibitor into the waters around the ruins.

Travel: The region adjoins Erinnyes Forest and Dryas Wood. The Callas Line aquabus route was shut after the explosion.

Quests: World quests include Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble (the start of the Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles), In Search of Lost Time, Villains, Ardent Calibration, Buried Honor, Road to the Singularity, Science of Data Management and Treacherous Light of the Depths.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the old laboratories remain in ruins and the Institute operates from the New location.

No newer content than 4.1 was found for this area.

86.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region: Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies
86.content: Large blocks of water left floating in the air after the explosion that devastated the Central Laboratory, in an institute whose research aimed to use Arkhium to defy gravity.

87.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region: New Fontaine Research Institute
87.content: The Institute's current building, built near the old ruins after the explosion. Former name: Alain Guillotin Research Institute. Raimondo and Choiseul run it as co-administrators in the quest Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble.

88.content:
Forbidden Zone: The Forbidden Zone is the hidden lowest part of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's undersea prison. It is built over Primordial Water, and a giant sluice gate there was made to stop that water from flooding Fontaine. Only the Fortress's Administrator, Wriothesley, may enter, and he reaches it by a secret stair from his office.

Prisoners tend to go quiet when asked about it, though the guards confirm that it exists. For years almost nobody remembered why the Fortress had been built, and the zone holds the answer.

Geography: A hidden staircase opens beneath the Duke's Office in the Administrative Area, and the office's basement has a lift down to the zone. Three large isolation doors lead into a chamber with the sluice gate and a bank of dashboards. A glass-walled room off the Duke's basement overlooks a huge ship under construction.

Places: The main chamber holds the sluice gate and the dashboards. Wriothesley watched the readings for years without knowing what they measured. A secret works nearby holds the Wingalet, a huge vessel he had built as a lifeboat in case the Primordial Water broke through.

Governance: Entry belongs to the Administrator alone. Wriothesley became Administrator and kept the zone from the inmates; even many of the people who worked on the ship were not told what it was for.

History: When exiles were first sent to the seaside in the age of the Hydro Archon Egeria, they began building the Fortress under her guidance to guard a secret deep beneath the waves. Their community grew into a home for sinners, and over centuries the reason for its founding faded from memory. Wriothesley learned it from an elderly research historian. As the prophecy says, if the gate fails, Fontaine will drown and all will dissolve into the sea.

Dangers: Primordial Water dissolved Fontainians who touched it, until the change of 4.2. In 4.1 it was seeping into the sea around the Fortress, and the Fortress was evacuated 'upwards and outwards' during the breach.

Quests: Revealed in the Archon Quest Chapter IV, Act IV, in 'Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones', after the Traveler answers Wriothesley's riddles about the Fortress's hidden rules. The breach is in 'Calamitous Tread' (4.1).

Status as of 7.1: Its sluice gate was resealed by Neuvillette in 4.1.

What became of the chamber after the flood of the prophecy is not described in the sources read; treat it as unknown.

89.content:
Fort Charybdis Ruins (also: Fort Charybdis, Mysterious Ruins of Fort Charybdis): Fort Charybdis Ruins are the remains of a fort on an island in the eastern part of the Morte Region. Inside lies a hidden underground complex, the Orthant of Wishes, which holds one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage placed by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The fort's name is also spoken by Remurian golems in 4.6 as a place where their legions were told to fall back. Canon text about the fort itself is thin.

The fort was introduced in Version 4.2 with the Morte Region and the World Quest chain In the Wake of Narcissus. The area is linked to the Ordo's diary notes and a hymn that Boethius later quotes.

Geography: An island ruin on the east of the Morte Region. The visible fort is a ruin on top of a "Wilderness Cavern" level, below which lies the Orthant of Wishes, a puzzle-filled chamber with several floors, mechanisms, energy flow pipes and an underwater section.

People: No named inhabitants. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo's members left behind a diary; the Ordo's founder Jakob Ingold and their leader, the Master, appear in it. Caterpillar and Ann help the Traveler find the seals.

History: No source describes who built the fort or why. The Ordo later used the site as one of four seals for its Great Ritual; the diary of a member records that the party found "Remuria's ruins" at the indicated location and arranged an official construction project.

The diary says the Palais Mermonia confirmed the location and a construction team arrived, with Marechaussee Hunters hired for security. The Master and Mr. Ingold brought an Oceanid to a tower not yet finished; later they said the Master was performing the Great Ritual, tied to celestial bodies and the Primal Fire (Phlogiston). Workers began spreading uneasy rumours, and a faction led by a woman called Zenaida left the Ordo, but the writer later found by divination that those who had left were still inside the tower.

Quests: In Meteoric Lance, part of Search in the Algae Sea, the Traveler enters the ruins, solves puzzles and reads the riddle slate to collect a wish piece for the seal. In both versions a man lies unconscious at the door and is taken to Lumidouce Harbor for treatment; the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's handiwork is suspected.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged since the 4.2 quest. The seal and the Ordo's apparatus remain.

Nothing newer than the 4.2 quest is known about the site.

90.comment: Fort Charybdis Ruins: Excerpt: Echoes Hallowed and Humble
90.content: An engraved hymn in the Mysterious Ruins, quoted as Movement 5, Stanza 3 of "Echoes Hallowed and Humble". It contrasts barbarians and witless water creatures with those whose strength comes from will, which they share with the noblest gods, and says the obedient rest bow down before those who command by will. A line in the Orthant of Memory, a different seal, quotes Movement 9, Stanza 37 of the same work, and Cassiodor quotes that second verse against Boethius in Fortune Plango Vulnera.

91.content:
Fortress of Meropide (also: Meropide): The Fortress of Meropide is a metal-walled stronghold under the sea in Fontaine's Liffey Region. It serves as Fontaine's de facto prison: people convicted at trial are sent there to serve their sentences. It is also the nation's largest maker of clockwork meka. Legally it governs itself. Convicts there count as exiles, and the Court of Fontaine has no jurisdiction beyond lending some Gardes for security. Inside, Credit Coupons replace Mora. The Administrator is Wriothesley, a former inmate who holds the honorary title of "Duke". The Melusine Sigewinne runs the infirmary.

To ordinary Fontainians the name is a byword for punishment ("I'll punch you straight into the Fortress of Meropide"). Its real founding purpose was forgotten for centuries: it was built to guard a sealed opening to the Primordial Sea.

Geography: The Fortress lies on the seabed off the Liffey Region, ringed by searchlights. Convicts reach it from River Talionis, a reception wharf beneath the Opera Epiclese. A lift behind the opera house descends to the wharf, and a boat carries them through an underground tunnel to the Fortress. A second entrance is reached from Erinnyes. Inside, its levels run from the Reception Area and the Dormitory Block down to the Administrative Area, two levels of the Production Zone and the Abandoned Production Zone.

Places: The Administrative Area is the hub, built around a central office. The Duke's Office stands at its centre. It has three floors: Wriothesley's office with a desk, sofa and tea table on top, and a basement with a lift to the forbidden zone. The Coupon Cafeteria serves meals. The Pankration Ring, reached by its own lift, is the Fortress's favourite entertainment. The infirmary, run by Sigewinne, is open to everyone at all hours. The Production Zone, two levels below the Administrative Area, is where inmates work.

People: Wriothesley, the Duke, rarely leaves the Fortress. He gets the information and resources he needs through his own network and treats inmates, guards and staff alike. Sigewinne, the Head Nurse, is a Melusine who came in as a convict and stayed after her sentence to care for everyone. The population is mostly inmates working off sentences, plus guards (some of them Gardes lent by the Court) and staff. Gardemeks also patrol.

Governance: The Fortress is formally autonomous and self-governing. Criminals sent there are technically exiles from Fontaine, and the Court cannot even investigate inside without the administrator's consent. In 4.1 Neuvillette had to send the Traveler in undercover. The Administrator holds all authority. Wriothesley runs the place through Mora, manpower and the right people, and comes down hard on anyone who exploits others. The Fortress sells meka to the surface, and the Palais Mermonia is one of its best customers, so he gladly satisfies the Maison Gestion's strict paperwork.

History: In the age of the first Hydro Archon, Egeria, Fontaine exiled its criminals and refused them help. Some repented and begged for mercy. Egeria forgave them and set them to guard her secret beneath the waves, and they built the first fortress. Later generations of exiles kept working on it long after the first had died. The secret was an opening to the Primordial Sea, sealed behind a sluice gate in a "forbidden zone" that only the warden and trusted people may enter. Over the centuries almost everyone forgot why the Fortress existed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fortress still operates as prison and factory under Wriothesley, with Sigewinne as Head Nurse.

Neuvillette resealed the breached sluice gate in 4.1. Since 4.2 Fontainians no longer dissolve in Primordial water. After the prophecy's flood the Wingalet went back into storage at the Fortress.

92.comment: Fortress of Meropide: Credit Coupons and the Welfare Meal
92.content: Credit Coupons are the Fortress of Meropide's internal currency and replace Mora for every transaction inside. Inmates earn them through work and spend them at the Coupon Cafeteria, the Rag and Bone Shop and elsewhere. With enough Coupons one can order meals to taste. Everyone gets one free Welfare Meal a day from the meka Bran: a surprise dish of unpredictable quality plus a fortune slip. It is the one equality in the Fortress that need not be bought.

93.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Forbidden Zone and the Sluice Gate
93.content: Beneath the Duke's Office, behind three large isolation doors, is a chamber with a giant sluice gate and gauges. Only the Administrator may enter. Wriothesley had long wondered what lay behind it. Over the year before the Traveler's arrival its gauge crept into the red. After Freminet collapsed from Primordial Seawater in the waters near the Fortress, Wriothesley concluded the gate held back the Primordial Sea. Inmates with historians' backgrounds had also argued to him that the sea which once swallowed Remuria might someday return. Soon afterwards the gate burst. Wriothesley held the water with Cryo ice, Clorinde shot a control panel to drop the security gates, and Neuvillette arrived, pushed the water back and resealed the gate.

94.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Traveler's Imprisonment
94.content: Childe, wrongly convicted by the Oratrice in the disappearances case, was sent to the Fortress and then vanished. The Knave asked for access, and Neuvillette, who has no jurisdiction inside, proposed a third party instead. He charged the Traveler and Paimon with eating a cake meant for Furina, and they were given 45 days. Wriothesley guided part of their tour himself. They found that a group of inmates who had come to follow Childe had invented a "hidden rule" about cannibals in the pipes to cover his escape: he had left through the pipes after hearing a "voice" again. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet were inside too, having got themselves imprisoned by staging a theft on the Knave's orders.

95.content:
Fountain of Lucine (also: Fontaine de Lucine, Lucine Fountain): The Fountain of Lucine stands in front of the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine. Fontainians say all of the nation's water ultimately gathers there, and it is the origin of the habit of tossing coins into fountains to make wishes. It has listened to Fontainians' wishes for a very long time.

In play it is also an offering system: Hydro Sigils gathered across Fontaine can be thrown into it to raise its level and earn rewards, and at the top level extra streams of water rise from its six corners.

Geography: A large ornamental fountain on the plaza before the Opera Epiclese, in the Court of Fontaine Region. A water-themed inscription is carved on it; in paraphrase it asks that no spring or fountain ever run dry and that the torrent of life wash over the valley. Rainbow Rose and Romaritime Flower grow nearby as local specialties.

Culture: Fontainians throw coins into fountains to make wishes, a custom a loading-screen text says truly began with tossing Hydro Sigils into this fountain, which it calls the correct way to wish. Newlyweds traditionally wish for children here, according to the Archon Quest chapter set in the city.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the fountain is intact and in ordinary use before the Opera Epiclese.

96.content:
Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe (also: The World's Amniotic Fluid): Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe is a stretch of the Primordial Sea, the ancient water beneath Fontaine, reached only during the world quest Waking from the Great Dream (4.2). It is the arena where the Traveler, Paimon and Ann face Narzissenkreuz, the failed leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

The quest places the Traveler in an ocean current that leads to a giant Hydro figure. Its in-game viewpoint is titled "The World's Amniotic Fluid", with the line that this was once meant to be the cradle of all life again.

Geography: The place is water and current rather than land. The Traveler enters an ocean current, keeps moving ahead, and reaches a giant being, Narzissenkreuz, in a Hydro-filled arena. During the fight, rift-like cracks and a bubble the Holy Blade points toward appear in the water. Healing orbs occasionally rise in the arena.

History: Narzissenkreuz sought to bring about a new world and so avert the apocalypse of the Prophecy of Fontaine, and took control of the Primordial Sea for that purpose. In the quest he claims to be saving the world and demands the Holy Blade. After he falls, he says he has lost all control of the Primordial Sea and that the new world cannot be born.

Atmosphere: Vast, dreamlike and ominous: deep water without a shore, a voice announcing that the day of return has come, and a being that speaks of salvation while attacking. The mood is one of a half-formed world, grief and a failed dream rather than ordinary menace.

Dangers: Narzissenkreuz fights with Hydro attacks in the form of water-made fists, spears, hammers and swords, and calls down a "Rain of Blades". For the quest the party is limited to a trial Traveler. Fontaine-born people dissolve in pure Primordial Seawater, while non-Fontainians only gain greater sensitivity to Hydro, according to the Primordial Sea page.

Travel: There is no ordinary route. The quest sends the party into the Primordial Sea by current. The viewpoint is only available by entering the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's hidden chamber through a book in a set spot, and its Archive entry stays hidden until collected.

Quests: Waking from the Great Dream, the single world quest of the third act of In the Wake of Narcissus (after Savior's Wake and before Rowboat's Wake). Completing it grants the achievement An Immortal Emperor in a Mundane Universe.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the place is known only from this quest. Narzissenkreuz was defeated there, and the story afterwards moves on to the resealing of the water and his later disappearance.

97.comment: Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe: Narzissenkreuz's Defeat in the Primordial Sea
97.content: In the Primordial Sea, Narzissenkreuz called the Traveler an equal to a world, only after the Holy Blade had cut through the will around him. Beaten, he said the Holy Blade was not on his side and that his ordinary self had returned to its body. Ann, whose soul he said was made of two colours, forgave him in her own right.

98.content:
Geode Mine Shaft (also: Arkhium Crystal Geode Mine Shaft): The Geode Mine Shaft is an abandoned mine in the Fortress of Meropide's abandoned production zone, filled with Arkhium crystal and patrolled by Flying Energy Thieves. It is the escape route used in the world quest An Eye for an Eye.

Mining stopped after the Fontaine Research Institute accident. A locking research terminal at the shaft's front opens only with two people working together, and the way out is rigged with a hazard.

Geography: Reached from the abandoned production zone level of the Fortress, beyond sluice gates and a pipe, in a setting that looks nothing like the rest of the Fortress: no signs of ordinary buildings, only rock, tunnels and glittering crystal.

Dangers: A Flying Energy Thief guards the shaft: a "trial product" that pursues anyone carrying an energy storage device and disables the device. The front research terminal needs such a device to start, so whoever activates it is chased.

History: Arkhium mining here halted after the Fontaine Research Institute accident. Later, guards had Clynes install a lock like the one at the Rift of Erosion; Clynes mentioned having prepared a "surprise" there, and the notice at the terminal describes the Flying Energy Thief.

Quests: In An Eye for an Eye (4.1, chapter Unfinished Comedy), Caterpillar decides to take Lanoire out of the Fortress and back to her family via this shaft. The Traveler and Paimon help, race the Flying Energy Thief and open the way out. On the other side Lanoire sees the open outdoors for the first time.

Status as of 7.1: Disused as a mine and known only as the route in the quest, as of 7.1.

99.comment: Geode Mine Shaft: Flying Energy Thief
99.content: A trial mechanism posted at the Geode Mine Shaft that hunts anyone carrying an energy storage device and disables it. According to the notice at the terminal it was never reviewed internally or by peers.

100.content:
Hidden Dwelling (also: Guillotin home): The Hidden Dwelling is the former home of Alain Guillotin and of his creations Sandrone and Pulonia. Its map description calls it a place where flowers and grasses flourish and time passes gently. It is a quiet house that bears witness to everything that unfolded in the 'home'. It becomes accessible in the 6.7 event story Those We Have Lost and stays open afterwards.

Sandrone, known to the Fatui as the Marionette, was brought to life here and later left. Alain Guillotin is the founder of the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering.

Geography: A house with a garden, a workshop area with a workbench, a fireplace with an old easy chair, a desk and Alain's bedroom, kept almost as it was when Sandrone left. In the event quest the party goes beneath Fontaine's waters, with the Wingalet as their base, and activates a water-insulating mechanism to reach it.

Places: The workbench is where both Sandrone and Pulonia were brought to life; later Sandrone worked on Pulonia there. A desk holds old maths toys and puzzles, among them the Pagoda Stack, a gear-moving puzzle. Alain's bedroom has a box with a hidden gear-locked compartment. By the fireplace sits an easy chair. The mechanical piano, which Alain once built, stood outside the house. A picture of Alain with Rene hangs in the house.

People: Alain Guillotin lived here, growing bedridden in his last years. He taught Sandrone mechanics and let her take over his workbench. Sandrone and Pulonia are described as his prime creations. The three are said to have kept a quiet, repetitive but peaceful life here, which Sandrone later called a world where time did not exist.

History: During Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7), Sandrone brings the Traveler and Paimon to the dwelling in the event quest Those We Have Lost to look for a gift Alain left behind. They find it in a hidden compartment in his bedroom. In the next quest, Those We Have Kept, the home is restored to a quiet state and Pulonia's body is returned to the workstation.

Dangers: No hazards are described. Sandrone only warns the Traveler to be careful with the old belongings and the dust.

Atmosphere: Still and gentle: flowers, fireplace and a dusty workshop. Sandrone's idle remarks as she wanders the house are brief, such as 'Old notes...', 'Pulonia...' and 'A warm hearth...'.

Travel: Freely accessible after Those We Have Lost. Teleport to the point of interest named Hidden Dwelling.

Quests: Those We Have Lost and Those We Have Kept, the second and third parts of Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7, a limited-time event).

Status as of 7.1: Quiet and open to visit as of 7.1.

Alain's piano stands outside again, Pulonia's inactive body is in the workstation, and the two pictures are back in the house.

101.content:
Hortus Euergetis: Hortus Euergetis (Latin, "Garden of Euergetis") is an underwater garden in Machimos, the outer city of Remuria in the Sea of Bygone Eras. It takes its name from Euergetia, a Harmost of Remuria who died in the kingdom's destruction. A short engraving at its waypoint, signed by Ouranides of Ouranopolis, wishes her peace and promises that flowers will always bloom for her here.

Introduced in Version 4.6 and visited in the quest The Last Day of Remuria. Hunter's Rays swim over it.

Geography: A subarea of Machimos, the outer city of the capital, near the Initium Iani, Caesareum Palace and Portus Anticus. The engraving sits on the upper north-east side of the teleport waypoint, at the base of a rock arch. The tall rock formations of Machimos are thought to be remnants of the old city.

People: Euergetia, called the benefactrix, was one of the four Harmosts of Remuria and is remembered as kindhearted. Her friend Cassiodor (writing as Ouranides of Ouranopolis) treats her as a sister. Boethius, another Harmost, is said in the Faded Castle's notes to have wished to revive Remuria with her after her death but failed.

Quests: The Last Day of Remuria lists the garden among the quest's subareas. No dialogue is tied to the garden itself.

Status as of 7.1: A quiet sunken memorial as of 7.1; nothing in later content changes it.

102.content: The engraving reads as a short elegy: it asks that the kindhearted Euergetia's melody find peace, calls her colleague, friend and sister, and says that though her beneficence and her name be forgotten, flowers will bloom for her here. It tells her to sleep and to weep no more, and to laugh as she once did.

103.content:
Hotel Bouffes d'ete (also: Hôtel Bouffes d'été, Hotel Bouffes d'été, the Hotel): Hotel Bouffes d'ete is a luxurious hotel in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine. It is legally owned by the Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino, called 'Father' by the orphans there, and is the base of her House of the Hearth in Fontaine. A children's home runs behind the hotel front. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet live there.

Its residents think of it as a family home. Its name means roughly 'Summer Bouffe Singers Hotel' in French.

Geography: In a corner of the Court of Fontaine in the Vasari Passage. Its story text mentions a grand hall with a phonograph, a small maintenance workroom and water-pumping equipment.

People: Current residents the wiki names are Lyney, Lynette, Freminet, Chapleau, Foltz and Heloir. Former residents include Filliol, Horrer, Jeambel, Landois, Lapouyade, Nanteuil, Sotto and Tadie. Arlecchino visits infrequently and is addressed as Father; the House's rule is that betrayal is not tolerated.

Governance: Arlecchino holds legal ownership and rules by her word. Orphans of the House carry the surnames Snezhevich and Snezhevna. The House's operations in Fontaine pursue what it calls a just cause but with radical methods, with Arlecchino's influence and her control over the inner workings of the Court of Fontaine preventing serious incidents, according to Lyney's profile.

Culture: Residents see the Hotel's festivals as the only warm events in their lives, since outside festivals feel cold and foreign to them. On its Founding Day the children decorate the hall with streamers, eat desserts and watch a magic show by Lyney, Lynette and Freminet.

History: The Hotel is the House of the Hearth's known Fontaine base. The House traces back to an orphanage in Khaenri'ah and was later refounded by an earlier Knave. Arlecchino took over after Crucabena, and wanted the children to call her 'Father'. In Lyney's Character Stories the twins arrive at the Hotel after tragic years and settle in.

Dangers: It is a Fatui front. Anyone who betrays the House faces death, though Arlecchino can spare people with a potion of her flame that erases their memories of the House.

Travel: A point of interest in the Vasari Passage. Sandrone's Portable Tea Table can be placed near the entrance to start the tea party quests Whispers by the Hearth and Tea Party Re-Invitation: House of the Hearth.

Quests: Appears in the Ignis Purgatorius Chapter (Arlecchino's story quest, requires the Archon Quest through Masquerade of the Guilty), in Lyney's profile, and in the tea party quests Whispers by the Hearth and its re-invitation.

Status as of 7.1: The House of the Hearth's Fontaine base, with Arlecchino as owner, as far as the sources read.

104.content:
Hotel Debord (also: Debord, Debord restaurant): Hotel Debord is a famous restaurant in Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine. Its owner, Vaneigem, holds that art is the best seasoning for good food and often invites performers to entertain diners.

The interior is designed so guests can see performances from any seat. It was founded long ago by the chefs Modeste and Savelli, and is tied to the Gateau Debord and the head chef Escoffier.

Places: Downstairs are the dining hall, with the host Sanguinetti and the hostess Leone; upstairs hold more staff including Argalia, Rodamonte, Renaud and the boss Vaneigem. Sanguinetti sells food, ingredients and recipes, with daily restocks; Reputation Rank 4 in Fontaine gives a permanent 10 percent discount (gameplay).

People: Vaneigem owns it, Sanguinetti hosts and the critic Eloise dines in the hall. Savanna is the current head chef. Escoffier, a former head chef, was also Furina's chef, and Monica is a former chef.

History: Modeste and Savelli, two chefs from Fleuve Cendre, made Fontainian cuisine popular through ingredients found on their expeditions and founded the restaurant, which was soon a hit with wealthy diners. About ten years later they found a container in sunken Remurian ruins whose contents sharpened taste, and Modeste created the original Gateau Debord, limited to sixteen orders a day.

Atmosphere: Opulent and theatrical: dining as spectacle, with performers and a polished kitchen behind it.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1) under Savanna's management.

key: Entrance of the Passage of Ianus
105.content:
Initium Iani (also: Entrance of the Passage of Ianus): Initium Iani (Latin, roughly "the beginning of Ianus") is the great gate between Machimos, Remuria's outer city, and Capitolium, its inner city. It leads to the Passage of Ianus, the only way between the two, and it was where the dragon Scylla was sealed. In The Last Day of Remuria, Scylla, freed after millennia, blasts it open so the Traveler, Paimon and Monsieur Os can reach the Domus Aurea.

Introduced in 4.6. The Remurian symphony ran through its golden waterways, which let Boethius's forces shut the gate and trap Scylla as he tried to break in.

Geography: A subarea at the edge of Machimos. Behind it a water current runs the full length of the Passage of Ianus into Capitolium. The gate is a stone door carved with seals, which fall away one by one when broken.

People: Scylla, the vishap Dragon Prince, is tied to this place by his sealing and his breakout. Cassiodor (as Monsieur Os) explains its history. The Harmosts Boethius and Euergetia are credited with the original sealing.

Quests: The Last Day of Remuria: Scylla, freed, calls the gate a glorified stone door and blasts through its seals while the group swims the Passage of Ianus. The Traveler must stay close to avoid falling stalactites.

Status as of 7.1: Broken open by Scylla during the 4.6 quests; the door swung shut behind the group. No later content revisits it.

106.comment: Initium Iani: The Engraving of Decimus
106.content: An engraving says that in his life he was Decimus, a humble slave, and today he is no different from the exalted Harmost, sunken to the bottom of the sea. The text does not name the Harmost or explain Decimus's role.

107.content:
Institute of Natural Philosophy (also: The Institute of Natural Philosophy, Submerged Ruins of the Institute, Liliacruces Forum ruins): The Institute of Natural Philosophy is a dilapidated underwater research facility that once belonged to an organisation of the same name led by Director Dwight Lasker. Much of its research is still preserved in the flooded ruin, including precursors of modern Fontainian technologies and the earliest experiments of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The Traveler first reaches it in the Version 4.0 World Quest Aqueous Tidemarks.

Its notes show a scientific community that was proud, quarrelsome and worried: young prodigies, a secret group forming among its leaders, and a warning of toxins and tainted Oceanids after a great disaster.

Geography: Submerged ruins in the Court of Fontaine Region, divided into Outskirts, a Central Quartier and a Northern Quartier, with a deeper underground wing. The Traveler enters by diving and finds sealed doors, ancient logs, glass walls and laboratory rooms.

People: Director Dwight Lasker; his childhood friends Basil Elton, Emanuel Guillotin and Karl Ingold; the young prodigies he recruited, including Coppelius, Alain Guillotin and Alain's assistant Carter Scherbius; and Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold, who joined Alain's lab and later founded the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. In the present, the guide Virgil leads the Traveler.

Governance: A Director ran the Institute and decided funding and admission. Dwight's notes show him approving research, increasing investment, assigning researchers to labs and receiving reports about members.

History: The Institute was a research body led by Dwight Lasker. During a cataclysm about five hundred years ago Dwight closed it for the safety of its people and kept the young from going to fight, urging post-disaster reconstruction first.

After the flood period began, he picked land near the Fountain of Lucine to relocate, only to hear that an opera house would be built there. He later met a newly appointed Iudex and judged him far more reliable than "Leon and those other clowns". Alain introduced Rene and Jakob Ingold, who turned out to be Karl's adopted sons; Dwight enrolled them and assigned them to Alain's lab despite the unrest it caused among other researchers.

Culture: The surviving texts mix science with legend, for example the origin of the Oceanids from Egeria's tear. The Institute valued child prodigies; Dwight says it is its responsibility to support gifted and talented youths.

Quests: Aqueous Tidemarks (4.0): the Traveler follows Virgil to find the Liliacruces Forum's treasure, discovers the Institute, defeats clockwork meka and a Ruin Guard, solves a key puzzle, and fights a "special" Ruin Grader in a vault before breaking a glass wall and following a current.

Status as of 7.1: Still flooded and abandoned. Its documents remain, and its oldest dangers are guarded by meka.

Nothing newer than 4.2 is known to have changed it.

108.comment: Institute of Natural Philosophy: Ancient Natural History Excerpts (Oceanids)
108.content: Excerpts of a natural-history text say that, by legend, Egeria shed the first tear and from it the first Oceanid was born, with the task of understanding all life. Oceanids differ greatly in intelligence and multiply by a mysterious "Helixsplit" after seeking permission from the Hydro Archon or an elder. A sceptical addendum notes that physical evidence suggests the Oceanids predate both Egeria and Remuria, and asks whether anyone dares explore their true origin.

109.comment: Institute of Natural Philosophy: Ancient Investigative Report (the Master)
109.content: A report in the deepest room mentions a suspected association among leaders and a "Master". The group is vigilant about outside investigation but not aggressive, so no official action was taken, and the writer suspects the Institute may be the hub.

110.content:
Lepaute Horlogerie: Lepaute Horlogerie is a clock shop in Quartier Lyonnais, owned by Caron. Horlogerie is French for clockmaking, and the shop stands near his older brother Livre's toy workshop.

Caron designs clocks and makes clockwork toys as a side business. Armand also appears at the shop.

Places: In Quartier Lyonnais, between Livre's workshop and the Fontaine branch of the Northland Bank on the same street.

People: Caron owns it. Armand is also found at the shop and stammers when he greets visitors; his role is not stated.

Atmosphere: A clockmaker's shop with a rival workshop a few steps away.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

111.content:
Leschots Clockwork Workshop (also: Leschots's workshop, Leschots Clockwork Shop): Leschots Clockwork Workshop is a toy shop in Quartier Lyonnais run by Livre, who makes mechanical clockwork toys.

The workshop sells toy birds, puppets, clockwork horses, trumpet-blowing blubberbeasts and penguins. The penguin designs are consignments by Freminet, whom Livre admires.

Places: In Quartier Lyonnais, next to the Fontaine Northland Bank and Lepaute Horlogerie, run by his younger brother Caron.

People: Livre is the boss; Alberre and Arbon are staff. Freminet is commissioned for toy designs.

Atmosphere: A toy shop full of clockwork creatures and a friendly sibling rivalry.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

112.content:
Liffey Region (also: Liffey): The Liffey Region is the part of Fontaine's map that holds the Fortress of Meropide, an underwater stronghold that serves as Fontaine's de facto prison and largest maker of Clockwork Meka. Its Administrator is Wriothesley, and the infirmary is run by Sigewinne. Foothills on the east side of Mont Esus also belong to the region.

Its boss is the Millennial Pearl Seahorse. The area is the setting for much of Archon Quest Chapter IV, Acts III to V, and a long run of world quests called Scenes from Life in Meropide.

Geography: The Fortress sits beneath the waters behind the Opera Epiclese and is reached by a lift down River Talionis. Around and inside it lie an Administrative Area, a Production Zone and an Abandoned Production Zone, a Forbidden Zone, a Geode Mine Shaft and a Dormitory Block. Mont Esus East is the eastern foothills of Mont Esus, which cannot currently be entered.

Places: - **Fortress of Meropide**: autonomous underwater stronghold; its own building entry gives full detail.
- **Administrative Area / The Duke's Office**: the offices of Administrator Wriothesley.
- **Production Zone and Abandoned Production Zone**: the factory parts of the Fortress; Clockwork Meka are made here.
- **Forbidden Zone**: a restricted area sealed since ancient times, closed to everyone except the warden and trusted people.
- **Pankration Ring**, **Coupon Cafeteria** and **Rag and Bone Shop** are other marked sites inside the Fortress.

People: Wriothesley is the Fortress's Administrator and Sigewinne, a Melusine nurse, works in its infirmary. Inmates, guards and staff appear throughout the Scenes from Life in Meropide quests. Outside the Fortress, Gardes provide some security support.

Governance: Technically an autonomous entity governing itself and outside Fontaine's legal system: criminals sent there are in effect exiles, and the Court of Fontaine only sends some Gardes to help with security. Wriothesley is its Administrator.

History: According to the wiki's compilation of the Fortress's lore, a group of exiled criminals first built it after Egeria began her rule in Fontaine. Shunned by society, some of them begged for mercy; Egeria heard them and told them to help protect her secret beneath the waves. The 'secret' was an entrance to the Primordial Sea, which they sealed and labelled the Forbidden Zone.

Atmosphere: The official map blurb calls the Fortress a metal-walled fastness that has kept a great many secrets over long years.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers, Treasure Hoarders and Clockwork Meka; the Frost and Wind Operatives and Fatui Pyro Agents are elite foes. The Millennial Pearl Seahorse is the region's boss.

Travel: The lift behind the Opera Epiclese down to River Talionis is unlocked in A Tea Party Most Thorny (4.1). The wiki lists several ways to enter the Fortress for the first time; the Archon Quest sends the Traveler in as an 'inmate'.

Quests: Archon Quest quests filed under the region include Fortress of Meropide (Act III), Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones, Calamitous Tread (Act IV), and Deluge of Wrathful Waters (Act V's first quest). The wiki also lists the Scenes from Life in Meropide series, Both Brains and Brawn, Underground Crime, Into the Sunlight, A Moment's Respite, The Proud 'Beret Society' and Wriothesley: Quite the Win.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fortress still operates under Wriothesley and Sigewinne.

Nothing newer than 4.2 was found for this area.

113.content: A restricted area at the heart of the Fortress, closed to everyone except the warden and trusted individuals. The wiki's lore text says it hides an entrance to the Primordial Sea that the first exiles sealed at Egeria's request. A separate Rift of Erosion lies west of the Dormitory Block and is called a potential danger.

114.content: The eastern foothills of Mont Esus, a mountain that is currently inaccessible. It belongs to the Liffey Region.

115.content:
Loch Urania (also: Urania Lake): Loch Urania is a lake in Erinnyes Forest, Fontaine, containing a large water vortex that forms a big bubble at the top. It starts out tainted by contaminated bacterial mats; clearing them calms the water and the sky.

It is the starting place of the world quest Furious Mouth of the Spring, part of The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes, where an enraged vishap and a small Melusine called Pahsiv guard a "key".

Geography: A lake in Erinnyes Forest with a giant vortex whose top forms a bubble. An altar sits near the "mouth of the spring" in the water, with a vishap lying beside it.

Dangers: The enraged Primordial Bathysmal Vishap by the altar attacks anyone who disturbs the altar. Before cleansing, the winds make approaching difficult.

Quests: Furious Mouth of the Spring (World Quest, 4.2) begins here. The Traveler subdues the vishap and meets Pahsiv, who speaks in a few repeated words. She asks for help gathering three keys (misty path to the south, the spring to the north, willows to the east) and taking them to the square in the west, to protect Erinnyes. The quest has variants depending on how many Teardrop Keys the player already has.

Status as of 7.1: Calm and navigable once cleansed; no later change is recorded as of 7.1.

116.content: Pahsiv is the name Paimon gives a small Melusine met at Loch Urania who speaks in short fragments ("Pahsiv" works as yes and "Melusine" as no in her usage). She guards keys with the vishap and asks the Traveler to help protect Erinnyes. She is a quest character; do not expand her beyond the quest.

117.content:
Lumidouce Harbor (also: Port de Lumidouce): Lumidouce Harbor is a coastal elevator and observation deck built into the side of a waterfall in Fontaine's Erinnyes Forest, much like Romaritime Harbor. It is a vital trading port for Fontaine, handling a large volume of international cargo, including tea from Qiaoying Village in Liyue and spices from Sumeru. For some years it has been underfunded and worn down, with its planned expansion and aquabus line stalled.

It also serves as a transfer point for illegal goods, and a few underground groups hold influence among the docks.

Geography: The harbor is a coastal elevator and observation deck built on the side of a waterfall. A run-down tavern, "The Rusty Rudder", stands a short distance northwest of it, and the lower levels and the ships there are where underground trading takes place.

Places: The main deck and elevator are where most harbor staff work. "The Rusty Rudder" tavern is where employees gather after work and where shady dealings are arranged. A noticeboard next to Cassigneul carries staff complaints, trade adverts and notices.

People: Cassigneul is the Lumidouce Harbor General Manager and handles the staff's complaints; she has promised to pay salaries from her own pocket if she has to. Others include the traders and staff Afsoon, Chourei, Crapet, Hilmer, Jalade, Kimpel, Mermet, Xing Cheng and, after An Expected Lie, Chaussivert, Fusilier and Lemarcq.

Governance: Day-to-day administration falls to Cassigneul, who took over from Doutey; the Maison Cardinalice is the body whose promised works (expansion, the aquabus line) have not started. The Spina di Rosula watches the balance of power among the underground groups and grew worried when senior members of the Club di Pantaloni Novita crime organisation were all arrested.

History: Until a few years before 4.2, Mr. Doutey oversaw the harbor and planned to expand it for ever-increasing trade. A fourth aquabus line connecting it to the Court of Fontaine was also designed, but was suspended after the death of Callas, its chief financial backer. Around then an unnamed event (probably related) led many employees, most of the navigators and Doutey himself to leave, and Cassigneul was assigned to replace him.

Dangers: Chiefly smuggling and crooked deals rather than open fighting. The harbor has been a key transfer point for illicit goods, such as imitation Sinthe. According to Chaussivert, bribery, fraud and betrayal have declined recently.

Travel: The harbor lies in Erinnyes Forest. No aquabus runs there yet: the Lumidouce Harbor line is planned but unbuilt. Tea from Liyue's Qiaoying Village and spices from Sumeru pass through it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lumidouce Harbor is still a stagnant but working port. No later canon changes its state.

Its expansion and aquabus line remain stalled, and staff are still short. Cassigneul keeps the harbor running on promises and her own pocket.

118.comment: Lumidouce Harbor: Chaussivert and the Harbor-Watcher's Crew
118.content: Chaussivert is the self-styled "Harbor-Watcher" of Lumidouce Harbor, a man of strict honesty who refuses dirty money. In An Expected Plan the Traveler meets him while chasing Nacker, who nearly blew up the Fontaine Research Institute; Chaussivert had been asked to smuggle someone out of Fontaine and refused. After the Traveler beats him in a scuffle, he helps track the shipment with his crew. He later loses his crew, apart from Lemarcq.

119.content: "The Rusty Rudder" is a run-down tavern northwest of Lumidouce Harbor where shady deals are made and people who are down on their luck gather. Harbor employees also drink there after work.

120.content:
Marcotte Station: Marcotte Station is the terminus of the aquabus Navia Line, serving the Erinnyes area.

Riders from the Court Region Waterway Hub take the Navia Line, run by Elphane, to reach it. The Opera Epiclese is the other stop on the same line.

Travel: It is reached by the Navia Line from the Court of Fontaine main station; the line was named for Navia and its planning followed her mother's death.

Status as of 7.1: Active at the cutoff (7.1).

121.content:
Mary-Ann Memorial Park: Mary-Ann Memorial Park is a small, once scenic park just south of the Central Laboratory Ruins, in the area of Fontaine given over to the Fontaine Research Institute. Most of its buildings were destroyed by the explosion that levelled the old Institute. Beneath its shallow pond lies Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory.

The park is where researchers pick through surviving papers in the quest "Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble" and where malfunctioning meka attack in "A Letter".

Geography: Lies directly south of the Central Laboratory Ruins in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region. It is a park laid out around a shallow pond, with broken machines, pipes, canvas sheets and storage drums strewn across it. Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory is under the pond.

People: Nacker, a former senior researcher who survived the disaster, leads the party through the park in the quest, together with the reporter Chronie and the Traveler. Chronie notes that before "Edwin's big screw-up" Nacker had been second only to Edwin Eastinghouse at the Institute.

History: The park's own origins are not told. It was damaged in the Institute explosion; the quest of 4.1 sends Nacker, Chronie and the Traveler to look for paper assets that may have survived. They find mostly detritus, plus one set of experimental results for a miniaturized personal recording device that Nacker expects will interest Maillardet, who has long wanted tiny gramophones inside Artificed Dancers.

Quests: "Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble" (Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles, 4.1) passes through the park while recovering assets. "A Letter" (4.1) sends the Traveler here to defeat three malfunctioning Recon Log Mek - Ousia before heading to the Academic Assembly Hall. The Daily Commission "Ardent Calibration" (4.1 to 4.2 per the wiki) is also set here.

Dangers: Malfunctioning clockwork meka, such as Recon Log Meks, roam the ruined grounds.

Atmosphere: Half a park and half a ruin: a pond and plants beside twisted pipes and crates, with a stillness left behind by the blast.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the park remains ruined and can be explored in the game. No rebuilding of the park or of the Central Laboratory is documented.

122.comment: Mary-Ann Memorial Park: Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory
122.content: An abandoned laboratory beneath the shallow pond of Mary-Ann Memorial Park. The wiki gives no description of its purpose or history beyond its location, so it should be treated as an unexplained corner of the Institute's grounds.

123.content:
Administrative Area (also: Meropide Administrative Area, Fortress of Meropide Administrative Area): The Administrative Area is the central hub of the Fortress of Meropide, the undersea prison-factory in Fontaine. The Duke's Office, belonging to the Administrator Wriothesley, stands at its centre. The Fortress's teleport waypoint is here, across from the office. Guards, inmates, shopkeepers and the doctor all pass through it.

Credit Coupons are the only currency, and the area contains the places where they are spent.

Geography: It lies below the Dormitory Block and above the Production Zone. The Duke's Office stands in its middle, and a waypoint opens across from it once the Fortress's first quest is under way. A lift from the area leads to the Pankration Ring.

Places: The Duke's Office has three floors: the Duke's own office on top with a desk, sofa and tea table, and a basement with a lift to the Forbidden Zone and a door onto a glass-walled room overlooking the secret ship. The Coupon Cafeteria serves meals and the free daily Welfare Meal. The Rag and Bone Shop is owned by Alvard. The Pankration Ring is the Fortress's entertainment venue.

People: Named NPCs include Alvard (Rag and Bone Shop owner), Arderne (doctor), Bran (Coupon Cafeteria staff, a clockwork meka), Wolsey (cafeteria supervisor), Monglane (receptionist), guards Camden, Estienne, Galvana, Galvaryet and Goncourt, Millereau (Mutual Aid Network advertiser), and Edwin Eastinghouse, a former senior researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute.

Governance: Wriothesley governs the Fortress from the central office. The Fortress is formally autonomous and runs on Coupons rather than Mora. The area is where the Coupon economy is felt: the cafeteria and the Rag and Bone Shop are here.

History: The area is the setting for the Traveler's 45-day sentence in Chapter IV Acts III-IV and the Fortress is also the setting of Wriothesley's story quest (4.1). In Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones, Wriothesley opens the hidden stair in his office to the Forbidden Zone.

Dangers: No specific hazards are described here. Guards are posted in the area, and Pankration bouts take place in the Ring.

Travel: Reached through the Fortress's reception, via a waypoint that appears in the first Fortress quest, or by being caught by searchlights outside. It connects downward by lift to the Production Zone.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1, with Wriothesley as Administrator.

124.content:
Production Zone (also: Meropide Production Zone, Fortress of Meropide Production Zone): The Production Zone is the work area of the Fortress of Meropide. It has two levels below the Administrative Area, joined by a lift in the east of the Fortress. Inmates work here, and further below, through a lift in the lower level, lies the Abandoned Production Zone.

The Fortress is described as Fontaine's largest maker of clockwork meka.

Geography: An Upper Level and a Lower Level, connected by a lift. A pool of water with wooden crates sits in the centre of the Production Zone. The Lower Level has a teleport waypoint and a lift down to the Abandoned Production Zone.

Places: Upper Level residents include Clynes, Grainville, Irus and Nelly. The Lower Level has Lechlade and Maupoil. A pool at the centre has three empty wooden crates; Grainville thanks anyone who clears them, because keeping the place clean counts as maintaining order, and gives Coupons.

People: The wiki's NPC list, without titles, is Clynes, Grainville, Irus, Nelly (Upper Level), Lechlade and Maupoil (Lower Level).

Governance: Under the Administrator's authority. Inmates earn Credit Coupons by working.

History: The zone appears in the world only from 4.1. The Abandoned Production Zone is closed off, with the Geode Mine Shaft suspended.

Dangers: No hazards are listed on the zone's page. During the Cerberus Chapter, Beret Society members were found here, and during the breach in Calamitous Tread guards at the Lower Level lift ordered everyone to evacuate upward and outward.

Travel: Take the lift in the east of the Fortress down from the Administrative Area.

Quests: Appears in Reborn in the Land of Grievances (Wriothesley's Cerberus Chapter Act I) and in the Archon Quest evacuation in Calamitous Tread (4.1).

Status as of 7.1: Operating as the Fortress's factory floor as of 7.1.

125.content:
Merusea Village (also: home of the Melusines, Melusine village): Merusea Village is the home of the Melusines, the small amphibious all-female people of Fontaine. It lies underwater, inside the body of the dead beast Elynas, and the game calls it "an adorable and mysterious village where even the chimneys bubble". It has no official leader. Very few humans ever visit, but those who do tend to enjoy it.

The village can be entered only from underwater, by diving near Elynas' skull or in the pool just above the Beryl Region Statue of the Seven. Most Melusines live here, though many who work in the Court of Fontaine now live in the city.

Geography: Merusea Village has a northern zone (on land, where most villagers are found) and a southern zone (underwater), within the colossal remains of Elynas that fill nearly all of the Beryl Region. Local plants include the Romaritime Flower and Beryl Conch.

Places: The village has human-inspired structures made long ago by the Melusines: street lamps (installed because visitors found the space darker than they were used to) and swing sets. A vendor, Xana, trades goods for mechanical "components".

People: Residents include Serene, Cosanzeana, Flo, Iara, Laume, Lutine, Rufina, Sedile, Sluasi, Verenata and Virda on land, and Glaisti, Granna, Puca and Thirona underwater. Xana is the vendor. Mamere, the artist, is a Melusine from here who could hear Elynas.

Governance: There is no official leader. Serene handles day-to-day matters informally.

Culture: Melusines eat Tidalga but also enjoy human food, and adore the Breacher Primuses that share Elynas' body. They respect Neuvillette as their ideal "father". A Newsstand Board notice in the Court of Fontaine says bathing in the waters around the village is calming and leaves skin soft and smooth.

History: About 400 years ago, in the battle between the Marechaussee Hunters and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo inside Elynas' remains, an explosion killed many and drove the mechanical parts of clockwork meka through the beast's body. The Melusines were born from those wounds, and Elynas, who was dead but still conscious, regarded them as his daughters and taught them how to make a home: Merusea Village.

Atmosphere: Bubbling chimneys, handmade street lamps and swing sets: the village feels gentle, secluded and a little strange. It was dark enough that the Melusines added lamps for human visitors, who tend to enjoy their stay.

Dangers: The village is safe for Melusines, since Breacher Primuses do not attack them, but the waters around Elynas' remains hold Breacher Primuses and Consecrated Beasts. Jakob's attempts to restart Elynas' heart once threatened the village.

Travel: Only from underwater: dive near Elynas' skull or into the pool above the Beryl Region Statue of the Seven. Humans seldom come.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Merusea Village remains a hidden, peaceful Melusine home with no leader. No later canon changes its state.

Elynas remains dead and his heart has not been restarted. Many Melusines live and work in the Court, and some visit the village on holiday.

126.content: Elynas is the vast creature whose remains hold Merusea Village. The Melusines call him "Father". An Abyss-infused creation of Rhinedottir (per the wiki's reading of the quest), he loved exploring the world but realised that his happiness hurt others, and he let himself die. After death he kept his consciousness and craved company. He thinks of the Melusines as his children, though most can no longer hear his voice.

127.content: Serene is an indigo-skinned Melusine with short brown hair and red eyes, one of the older villagers, who sees herself as the others' big sister. Her open-world dialogue shows her helping with everyone's troubles.

128.content:
Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnéqui, Automnequi): Mont Automnequi is one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, a mountain that straddles two regions: its west slopes lie in the Belleau Region and its east slopes in the Morte Region. Much of Fontaine is covered by water, but this is one of the places where mountain and forest show through. From its heights one can look across to the ridge of Elynas and the lakes beneath which the Melusines' homeland is hidden.

A tunnel, the Poisson Tunnel, was dug through the west side so that the Clementine Line of the aquabus system could pass, a feat of the Fontaine Research Institute.

Geography: Mont Automnequi spans the Belleau Region (the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi, released in 4.0) and the Morte Region (the East Slopes, released in 4.2). The west side faces the coast where half of the wrecked Sponsian lies, with the Elton Trench just offshore and the ridge of Elynas across the water.

Places: Poisson Tunnel on the west slopes; a stretch of coast where wreckage of the Sponsian can be found; and, nearby, the Elton Trench offshore. The viewpoint "View From Mont Automnequi" stands on the west slopes.

History: The Fontaine Research Institute brought in huge engineering devices to bore the Poisson Tunnel, which the official map text calls one of the biggest challenges in building the aquabus lines. The wiki records that new machines, including the "Golden Vessel", were developed for the job.
