Quests: Canticles of Harmony (4.6): Prelude "The Shadow Over Petrichor" (Faded Castle), First Movement "Underwater Nocturne", Second Movement "The Last Day of Remuria" (freeing Scylla and breaking through the Initium Iani), Third Movement "Gradus ad Capitolium" (restoring the golden aqueducts) and Finale "Fortune Plango Vulnera" (the battle in Domus Aurea and the Requiem).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sunken capital is quiet: Phobos was destroyed in 4.6, the trapped Remurian souls have passed on and Scylla is free in the deep.

The Symphony mechanism still works for exploration, and golem guards remain. Cassiodor and Boethius are gone. Later versions refer back to Remuria in lore texts, such as the Temple of Space (6.5) and the Belyi Tsar's notes in Pale Crown Palace (7.0).

198.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Capitolium and Domus Aurea
198.content: Capitolium was the inner city of Remuria's capital, open only to the finest scholars and musicians, and only a few of them served the God King directly. At its centre, on the hill Clivus Capitolinus, stands Domus Aurea, a golden palace of tall copper pillars built as a giant harp-like instrument for playing Phobos. Remus sat at its heart, listening for any wrong note anywhere in the empire and correcting it with a pluck of his strings. Scylla calls the city the "Eternal City" and says Remus' will still protects it. In 4.6 Boethius made his last stand inside the palace, and the Traveler played the Requiem in its throne room, the Sacellum Requietis.

199.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Machimos and the Initium Iani
199.content: Machimos was the outer city of Remuria's capital, home of its warriors, with arenas, temples, gold-and-glaze walls and busy markets. The Initium Iani was the only gate into Capitolium, opening onto the Passage of Ianus. Boethius and the Harmost Euergetia sealed Scylla there by shutting the gate on him as he tried to break through. In 4.6 the freed Scylla broke the gate's stone seals and carried the Traveler through the trench beyond.

200.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Caesareum Palace
200.content: A training ground of the Remurian legions where the chains that held Scylla were kept. Boethius ordered Legio VI Rithimi Versi of the Legion Athanatoi to hold back the Dragonborn here; its records say no soldier deserted and no enemy got through. A nameless stone statue still offers a challenge to visitors.

201.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Portus Anticus
201.content: Remuria's royal port, now sunk into an underwater cavern. Ships came in past the Ocean Pillars along the royal fairway. Its tall bell tower was said to stand at the border of reality and dreams: its bell could "pierce the barrier of ocean" and lead sailors lured to sleep by sirens back home through the mist. The imperial ship Fortuna was berthed here.

202.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Alta Semita
202.content: A huge aqueduct shaped like a harp that once carried Ichor from Domus Aurea to "the great lake in the far north". Scylla remembers swimming in those waters. It broke apart after the fall. In 4.6 the Traveler restored it with fragments of the Symphony so that Domus Aurea's gates could be opened.

203.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Collegium Phonascorum
203.content: Remuria's centre of learning, where Harmosts and music teachers taught citizens the theory of the Symphony. Scylla calls its scholars "mad believers" who tried to bring non-human creatures under the Golden Symphony, creating the Auric Anglerfish.

204.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Hortus Euergetis
204.content: An undersea garden named after the dead Harmost Euergetia, called "the benefactress". An engraving signed "Ouranides of Ouranopolis" (Cassiodor's alias) mourns her as colleague, friend and sister, and promises that flowers will always bloom there for her even if her name is forgotten.

205.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Scylla in the Sea of Bygone Eras
205.content: Scylla is a giant vishap prince who led Dragonborn vishaps and "barbarians" against Remuria. Boethius trapped him in stone at the Initium Iani, and he stayed chained for millennia. Thoughts escaping from his stony prison took the form of a large glowing fish that swam past the Faded Castle's windows. The Traveler, Paimon and Cassiodor broke his three chains in 4.6, and he helped them reach Domus Aurea and complete Remus' Requiem. Proud, booming and friendly, he calls the Traveler and Paimon "little ones" and despises Boethius. He now roams these waters freely and asks the Traveler to visit him.

206.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: The Symphony and Phobos
206.content: The "Symphony" is human memory and persona woven into music, a melody in which souls can live and have their wishes granted. Sybilla, the Great Golden Bee and a prophet who survived an earlier cycle, taught the secret to Remus. He poured these melodies into Ichor, which the primordial sea could not dissolve, so that people could rule their own fates. Overwhelmed, the people asked to be guided, so Remus wrote every melody into one great Symphony: Phobos. Phobos turned out to have Sybilla's selfless urge to make "everyone" happy, so it tried to grant even its Remurians' wishes to conquer. The Symphony's remaining power still moves the ruins (the Symphony mechanic) and feeds the area's strange creatures.

207.content:
Secret Vault (also: Marechaussee Hunter vault): In the story quest Buried Honor, the group of Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney and the Traveler plays a tabletop adventure whose "treasure" turns out to be real Hunter heritage. The vault's door needs four keys, passed down through generations of Hunters, to form the complete key. What lies inside is no gold: a tablet and worn weapons, which the characters understand to be the Hunters' true legacy. It first appeared in Version 4.7.

Geography: Entrance east of the Central Laboratory Ruins, hidden by a rock that can be blown open; beyond lies a water-filled cave and then a quiet narrow passage ending at a stone door with a pattern mechanism.

People: Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney and the Traveler open it; Florian, a Hunter descendant, intended to seize it.

Dangers: In the quest, explosives had been planted in the cave; Clorinde dismantled them. The path also includes a fight with a possessed Florian.

Atmosphere: Hushed and ancient; the writing describes it as so quiet that the secret there seems to breathe.

Quests: Buried Honor, part 3 of the Silent Night act in Clorinde's story chapter (Rapperia Chapter).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it stays accessible as an exploration point holding the Hunters' tablet and weapons.

208.content: Four keys, each entrusted to a respected Marechaussee Hunter and passed down, combine into the complete key that opens the Secret Vault door. Florian stole three; Clorinde held the fourth.

key: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars
209.content:
Shadow of Another World (also: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars): Shadow of Another World is a Trounce Domain in Salacia Plain, Fontaine, unlocked after completing the Archon Quest "Finale". It lets the Traveler relive the battle against the All-Devouring Narwhal, the beast from another world. Its flavor text says that battle was the intersection of this world's fate, that Fontaine now treads a brighter path, and that the giant's whale-song will not fade from memory.

The fight is titled "Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars". It rewards weekly-boss materials: Lightless Silk String, Lightless Eye of the Maelstrom and Lightless Mass.

Places: The domain is a recreated arena rather than a place with its own geography. The recollection is reached from Salacia Plain.

Dangers: The All-Devouring Narwhal and the dark shadow within its belly. Hostility builds as the player strikes the beast or destroys the Eye of the Maelstrom, until the narwhal devours a character; defeating the shadow inside weakens it.

Quests: Unlocks after the Archon Quest "Finale" in Chapter IV, whose final battle it recalls.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent boss domain as of 7.1, added in 4.2; no new story events occur in it.

210.content:
Thalatta Submarine Canyon (also: Thalatta Canyon): The Thalatta Submarine Canyon is an underwater subarea of the Court of Fontaine Region, within the map level of the Source of All Waters, the Great Fontaine Lake. Its name uses "Thalatta", the Attic Greek form of the word for sea. It debuted in Version 4.0.

Canon records only exploration content here: a group of Hunter's Rays with an impostor among them, and one of the seven Mysterious Cores.

Geography: The canyon lies below the surface of the lake, so a scene there is a submerged one, with Hunter's Rays swimming between Teleport Waypoints. The wiki gives no description of its walls, depth, size or named landmarks.

Dangers: An Underwater Survey Mek hides among a group of Hunter's Rays. Defeating it unlocks the hidden achievement "Like Tears in the Rain", whose name references the film Blade Runner.

Quests: No quest is recorded in the canyon. One Mysterious Core, a quest item from chests after completing seven Pneumousia puzzles, is placed here as the seventh. The cores are handed to Henri to begin "Still Mouthwatering!", a quest set elsewhere.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is accessible and has no known story events.

211.content:
The Duke's Office (also: Duke's Office, Wriothesley's office): The Duke's Office is Wriothesley's office, in the centre of the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide. Its door is often shut tight, yet its owner knows everything that happens in the Fortress. It has three floors.

The top floor holds Wriothesley's desk and a sofa with a tea table; in Chapter IV of the Archon Quest it is where the Traveler comes to ask him for answers about the Fortress. A basement opens later and holds a lift to the Forbidden Zone.

Geography: The office has three floors. The top floor is the working office, with a desk and a sofa with a tea table. The basement floor becomes available during Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones and contains a lift down to the Forbidden Zone and a door to a room overlooking a ship, the Wingalet. After Masquerade of the Guilty the door stays open but the ship is gone.

People: Wriothesley, the Duke, works here. Sigewinne, the Fortress's medical officer, comes by in the quest to check on Clorinde, and Freminet's recovery is mentioned. The quest also features Jurieu and Lourvine.

Governance: The Administrator of the Fortress of Meropide is known as the Duke. The Fortress is autonomous, and Wriothesley's reforms since taking over its administration are described on his own entry; this office is where he receives visitors and makes decisions.

Quests: In Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones (Chapter IV, Act IV, Part 3 of the Archon Quest) the Traveler comes to the office to question Wriothesley directly, then follows him through the newly opened basement lift into the Forbidden Zone. Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2) later changes the basement room.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the office is unchanged in the sources read.

212.comment: The Duke's Office: The Duke's Office
212.content: The Duke's Office is Wriothesley's three-floor office in the centre of the Fortress of Meropide's Administrative Area. Its door is often shut, but he knows all that happens in the Fortress. The top floor has his desk and a tea table; the basement, opened in Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones, has a lift to the Forbidden Zone and a door to a room overlooking a ship.

213.content:
The Narzissenkreuz Ordo (also: Narzissenkreuz Ordo chamber): The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, as a place, is the hidden meeting chamber of the secret society of the same name. It sits at the top of the Tower of Ipsissimus in Fontaine. In its ceiling is a Doomsday Clock made by the mage Narzissenkreuz to count down to the apocalypse of the Prophecy of Fontaine.

The chamber is now empty of ceremonial items and has not seen a Dispelling Ritual for a long time, but Caterpillar recognises it as the place where the sinners of Fontaine once gathered. Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour use it as a base while looking into the Ordo's past. The map text calls it a place where great dreams were once born and countless souls melted.

Geography: The chamber is an instance entered by choosing "Read" on a book at the end of the Institute of Natural Philosophy's Central Quartier; the first entry unlocks it as a waypoint on the map. A second book on a music stand inside lets the player leave. Its ceiling holds the Doomsday Clock, and a large circular window lights the room.

People: The Ordo's former members and leaders are described in their own entries. In the room today are Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour, who investigate the Ordo here. Caterpillar says he belonged to the Ordo but not to its inner circle, and that he was personally mentored by Narzissenkreuz.

Culture: Two notes found in the chamber after Search in the Algae Sea show the Ordo's outlook: one explains a ritual line about sinking into the great sea to be reborn, tied to a play about Ajax and an ancient Sumeru text phrase read as "primordial human"; the other argues that to excise the self is to die before death, so one can avoid receiving a Vision, which it treats as selling oneself to the fate of the world.

History: The society formed after its founders learned of the coming destruction of the world, and held that merging many wills into one being was the way to survive it. Their later work, including research on the Primordial Sea, leads on to the events investigated in Search in the Algae Sea. See the faction entry for details.

Quests: Riddles Awaiting Answers begins automatically when the Traveler first enters the chamber after Unfinished Comedy. Search in the Algae Sea, the only world quest of In the Wake of Narcissus Act I, is started here by talking to Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour two in-game days after Initial Facts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chamber is unchanged in the sources read, serving as the investigators' base.

214.comment: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo (chamber)
214.content: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, as a location, is the hidden meeting chamber of the secret society at the top of the Tower of Ipsissimus. Its ceiling holds a Doomsday Clock made by the mage Narzissenkreuz to count down the apocalypse. It is entered via a book at the end of the Institute of Natural Philosophy's Central Quartier.

215.content:
"The Real Annapausis" (also: The Real Annapausis): "The Real Annapausis" is the hidden heart of Annapausis, reached after Ann's storybook quest to rescue Princess Lyris. It is where the consciousness of Mary-Ann, a hybrid Oceanid, resides. First entered in the world quest "Mary-Ann's Story" (4.0), it then closed until "Rowboat's Wake" (4.2) made it permanently accessible.

The place looks like a gentle garden and school hall where Mary-Ann keeps tea, flowers and a "dog" waiting for visitors. It is, in her own words, a tomb rather than a home.

Geography: Part of the Annapausis subarea in the Court of Fontaine Region. It is reached by escaping the "Convoluted Corridor" of the adventure and has its own map entry. Inside are a flower garden, a tea hall that rings a bell for teatime, and a doghouse; at the end of the first visit the room floods.

People: Mary-Ann lives here. She appears as a young woman with fair skin, bright blue eyes, mid-length blue hair and a blue-and-white frilled dress. She is a hybrid Oceanid formed when Lyris absorbed the dying Mary-Ann Guillotin's consciousness, and the wiki says she unintentionally created the Oceanid Ann out of parts of her memories and dreams. Ann, Paimon and the Traveler meet her here.

History: Per the wiki, during a conflict in the remains of Elynas 400-500 years ago between the Marechaussee Hunters and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, Mary-Ann Guillotin was gravely wounded by an explosion. Lyris dissolved her and absorbed her consciousness, creating Mary-Ann. Mary-Ann presumed her old companions dead and built a dream in Annapausis, hiding inside a fairy tale the human had once told Lyris and waiting for the Institute's people to return.

Quests: "Mary-Ann's Story" (Ann of the Narzissenkreuz Act III, 4.0) and "Rowboat's Wake" (In the Wake of Narcissus, 4.2). After the latter, returning to the Real Annapausis and approaching the house grants an achievement.

Atmosphere: Warm, pretty and tinged with unreality: tea set out for guests who are not coming, flowers waiting to bloom, food that tastes like water, and a temperature that drops sharply when the dream breaks.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the place is open and empty of its resident. Mary-Ann set out after "Rowboat's Wake" with Ann, Seymour and Mamere to see the world beyond the glass wall, saying the garden is somewhere they can come back to if afraid.

216.comment: "The Real Annapausis": Mary-Ann Guillotin and Annapausis
216.content: The human Mary-Ann Guillotin was the sister of Alain Guillotin; the Oceanid Mary-Ann is a different, hybrid being that has her memories fused with Lyris'. The Real Annapausis is her constructed refuge. Ann, a young Oceanid born from the dream, believes her purpose is to rescue Princess Lyris, a quest Mary-Ann gently frees her from.

217.content:
The Wingalet (also: Wingalet, Wingalet Gloop-Gloop Funderwater Fisharium): The Wingalet is a very large ship that Wriothesley, administrator of the Fortress of Meropide, built in secret in the Forbidden Zone beneath the prison. He began it once he suspected the Primordial Sea lay just beyond the Fortress's sluice gate, meaning it as an escape vessel and something for Fontainians to hold on to. It surfaced during the Prophecy of Fontaine to rescue people from the flood, then went back into storage. In Version 6.7 it was leased out during the Fontinalia Film Festival and fitted with an aquarium.

Wriothesley modelled the project on the legendary Fortuna, the ship of Remuria's first king, though he did not expect it to match that legend.

Geography: Built in a factory-scale production zone of the Fortress of Meropide, below the Duke's Office and near the isolation gates of the Forbidden Zone. Wriothesley shows it to the Traveler and Paimon as a gargantuan silhouette seen through glass in the distance. When it rises, its sides open and cranes extend with hooks to haul people from the water.

History: Some years before the Traveler reached the Fortress, Wriothesley began to suspect that the Primordial Sea lay under the sluice gate he had found. He launched the project in secret so that Fontainians would have a way to reach safety and something to cling to, drawing on a whole factory's labour, materials and technology, with technical advice from Jurieu and Lourvine of the Fontaine Research Institute. The Traveler learns of it in "Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones" (Cataclysm's Quickening). Wriothesley warns that if the Fortress's workers learned the truth behind the ship, riots could destroy the Fortress faster than the catastrophe. When the Prophecy of Fontaine came to pass and the nation flooded, he commanded the Wingalet, which rose from the water to rescue the stranded. After the Prophecy was averted, it returned to the Fortress's factory and sat idle.

People: Wriothesley commands and controls it. Jurieu and Lourvine, former Fontaine Research Institute researchers working for him as technical consultants, advised on the design. Inmates of the Fortress clean and maintain it. In 6.7 Sandrone leases it under the surname Guillotin and is called its current captain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Wingalet belongs to the Fortress of Meropide and, since 6.7, doubles as an aquarium that Wriothesley agreed to keep running in part.

At the end of "Those We Have Kept" Wriothesley asks Sandrone, the current captain, whether some installations may stay so Fortress inmates can enjoy the aquarium, and she agrees. No later use of the ship is shown in canon through 7.1.

218.content: The Wingalet was built beneath the Fortress of Meropide as insurance against the Primordial Sea breaking through the sluice gate of the Forbidden Zone. Wriothesley hid it from the Fortress's own population so that panic would not spread. He admits it is no match for the legendary Fortuna, the ship on which King Remus founded Remuria with the seer Sybilla, but it gave Fontaine something to hold on to. During the Prophecy of Fontaine it was used for rescue work under his command.

219.comment: The Wingalet: Sunny Summer Fontinalia and the Wingalet Fisharium
219.content: During the limited Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (Version 6.7), Wriothesley rents the Wingalet out for the Fontinalia Film Festival to cover its upkeep and boost morale among the inmates who maintain it. The renter is a deep-pocketed woman with a fishing permit and business licence who sets up an aquarium; she turns out to be Sandrone, who uses the cover in the hope of finding the underwater home she shared with Alain Guillotin. Xavier and Lepine-Pauline's two film crews share the ship as a location. In the event the player runs the aquarium by collecting creatures and curios, and event rewards include a banner and a rules sign from the Fisharium.

220.content:
Tower of Ipsissimus (also: Tower of Gestalt, Sealed Ruined Tower): The Tower of Ipsissimus, also called the Tower of Gestalt or the Sealed Ruined Tower, stands in Fontaine's Morte Region. The secret society known as the Narzissenkreuz Ordo built it as its base. The Court later declared the Ordo an illegal extremist group and sealed the site. The tower is the way down to a seal over the Primordial Sea, and it sinks beneath the water for good after the 4.2 world quest Savior's Wake.

Its name comes from an old Remurian idea of a will powerful enough to rule, sustain and destroy the world. Its other names, such as Gestalt, point to the Ordo's goal of merging many wills into one.

Geography: A tall tower with a clock face high on it, rising from the Morte Region. Inside it has a top, a middle and a bottom level, each with its own puzzle, and below the bottom level lies the sealed way to the Primordial Sea. A hidden meeting chamber, also called the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, sits at the top and has a Doomsday Clock set into its ceiling.

Places: Each level carries exhibit-style panels and certificates for Ordo members, plus optical couplers (an Ordo design) used for puzzles. Notes describe the tower as a model of the evolution of the human soul. The bottom level holds a storybook with comments in purple ink, and a long investigation log about studying ruined temples and ancient Remurian script.

People: The Ordo was founded over 400 years ago by Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold, former members of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, and led by Narzissenkreuz. Jakob personally confronts the Traveler at the top of the tower. Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour come to the tower with the Traveler.

Governance: Members were grouped in clearance levels from one to four, with honorary levels for supporters who could not pass the tests. A notice on a wall panel high in the tower, carrying the seal of the courts and the signatures of Alain Guillotin and Neuvillette, declares the Ordo an illegal extremist group and criminal organisation under Fontainian law and the Mermonia Act, and orders the site sealed permanently. Destroying the notice board would count as a challenge to national authority.

History: The Ordo, formed after the All-Devouring Narwhal devoured the Primordial Sea, held that the world's destruction was coming and that the only escape was to merge people's wills into one transcendent being. It used the Tower of Ipsissimus as its base while it studied the Primordial Sea beneath. In Search in the Algae Sea (4.2) the Traveler is taken to the top of the tower, where Jakob demands a component of the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz. After a fight the blade is forged, and the Doomsday Clock strikes twelve and crushes Jakob.

Dangers: Clockwork meka of 'Special Order 172' wake at the lowest level when the seal is broken. The Primordial Sea beneath is dangerous.

Travel: The tower is on the ground close to a teleport waypoint. After Savior's Wake it is permanently underwater, so the structure cannot be walked through again.

Quests: The world quest series In the Wake of Narcissus (4.2) covers Search in the Algae Sea, Savior's Wake, Waking from the Great Dream and Rowboat's Wake. Savior's Wake is the quest that takes place in the tower itself.

Status as of 7.1: Sealed by the courts and, since 4.2, permanently submerged.

221.content:
Vasari Passage (also: Court of Fontaine: Vasari Passage): Vasari Passage sits at the bottom (south) of the Court of Fontaine. Streets lined with shops lead toward a large fountain plaza, and a cafe and several vendors serve passers-by.

It is one of the capital's shopping districts and a common meeting spot because of the statue plaza.

Places: Statue Plaza, the large fountain square where the shop streets converge; the Eastern Street and the Western Street; and Cafe Lucerne, managed by Arouet. Vendors include Boucicaut (Damoville Purveyor), Estelle (Beaumont Workshop), Eugenie (fresh produce) and Louis (snack shop).

People: Listed residents include Sanin, Nolette, Wei Xiaobao, Estella, Manet and Olivier, and Chatelet, Gontharet and Menthe at Cafe Lucerne.

Atmosphere: Shop windows, a plaza fountain and the steady foot traffic of a capital's commercial heart.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded.

222.content:
Weeping Willow of the Lake (also: Erinnyes's Watery Weeping Willow, Saule pleureur du lac): The Weeping Willow of the Lake is a large willow growing at the centre of a lake in Erinnyes Forest, its roots apparently reaching under the water. Fontaine's lore treats it as a barometer: it flourishes or withers as the water veins run sweet or bitter.

In ancient times it was an object of reverence. The viewpoint text laments that omens arrive only in the same month as calamity.

Geography: A lakeside subarea in Erinnyes Forest. Before the Roots of Erinnyes are cleansed in "The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes", the whole lake area looks a sickly yellow and the willow is tainted; afterwards it is a vibrant blue. The map reflects the change.

Culture: The viewpoint calls it revered in ancient times, tying the willow's flourishing or withering to the water being sweet or bitter and treating it as an omen, though one that comes too late.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lake and willow are healthy after the cleansing of the Roots of Erinnyes in 4.2.

223.content:
West Slopes of Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnequi West): The West Slopes of Mont Automnequi are the western side of one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, in the Belleau Region; the east side lies in the Morte Region. The slopes are known for the Poisson Tunnel, which carries the Clementine Line through the mountain, and for the clockwork inventor Antoine. Added in Version 4.0.

Official exploration text calls Mont Automnequi one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, noting that although much of the nation is covered by water, mountains and forests exist too.

Geography: Mountain slopes in the Belleau Region. The Poisson Tunnel passes through them. Local specialties include Lumidouce Bells and Rainbow Roses, and the wiki lists a viewpoint and a fishing point here.

Places: Poisson Tunnel: carved through the slopes for the Clementine Line. The Fontaine Research Institute built it with enormous machines, including a bore called the "Golden Vessel". The project's success spurred a new generation of clockwork technology, including the Construction Specialist Mek, which was based on the Golden Vessel.

People: Antoine Roger is an open-world NPC engineer here. He is the creator of the Miraculous Antoine Roger Aircraft found around Fontaine, and one stands near him. He believes humans should break free of the earth and soar, and he contrasts his clockwork flight work with Edwin Eastinghouse's research.

Dangers: Enemies include Hilichurls and Hydro Hilichurl Rogues, Treasure Hoarders, large Hydro Slimes, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasms and several types of Mek. The boss is the Emperor of Fire and Iron.

Quests: Quests listed for this subarea include "A Lady's Invitation", "Days Beneath the Waves", "Sea Breeze Rendezvous", "Still Mouthwatering!", "Truly Mouthwatering!", "The Art of the Elegant Blade Dance?", "Blade Dance's Unexpected End!" and "Studies in Light and Shadow: A Fontaine of Enchantment". Their stories are not covered here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the slopes are accessible and unchanged.
